correctness.rationale: A graph with two initial blue vertices cannot force beyond a single arm. For triples, a legal first force either uses a terminal plus a near-terminal arm vertex, or two consecutive internal vertices. Inspecting the remaining third seed yields exactly the two listed classes; propagation explicitly proves sufficiency. Disjoint enumeration gives 18+12(l-2). A direct exchange chain makes all minima connected. Slide moves preserve the occupied-arm pair at length three, where the displayed ten-state cycle is complete; for lengths at least four every adjacent move violates the classification. The extracted standalone checker independently exhausts every triple for lengths three through twelve, confirms minimum cardinality, and checks exchange/slide graphs. No finite computation is substituted for the proof.

originality.rationale: The precise claim is the exhaustive classification and count of all labelled minimum configurations of equal-arm theta graphs together with the sharp token-slide phase (three ten-cycles at length three and complete isolation for all greater lengths) despite continued token-jump connectivity. The 2019 degree-three theorem already covers the numerical minimum three and is not claimed as new. The 2020 token-exchange paper defines and studies the model for other graph families; the 2022 TAR paper uses a different move. Targeted theta-specific searches of public literature and indexed mathematical findings found no theorem implying this complete configuration-and-slide classification. The separate selected-arm support and consecutive-pair mechanisms are mathematically different from the circular-ladder zero-forcing classifications. This is a best-knowledge judgment, not proof of priority.
residual_risks: An unindexed paper or computational table might classify theta minimum zero forcing sets under another name.
Full literature beyond the inspected primary papers and indexed resources has not been exhaustively cleared; independent priority review is not performed.

value.rationale: The theorem resolves the entire optimum-configuration space on a canonical symmetric family of three-path theta networks. It exhibits a mathematically sharp discontinuity: subdividing each arm once at the length-three boundary freezes every local optimum-preserving move, while global one-token exchanges remain connected. That structural local-versus-global obstruction and its exact three-cycle exception are not routine consequences of knowing Z=3 or of arbitrary enumeration.
